The corpus covers this topic only in part. The RBI NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 bar harassment and harsh recovery methods, and say NBFCs must train recovery agents on "hours of calling" (para 98). Para 91 lists calling "the borrower befo[re]..." among practices deemed harsh, but the retrieved excerpt is cut off, so I could not confirm the specific contact-hour window (the 8 am to 7 pm figure in your search hint is not verified here). The full text of paras 91 and 100 is needed to confirm it.

What the retrieved passages say:
- **Harassment (para 100):** NBFCs must ensure they and their agents do not use intimidation or harassment, verbal or physical, in debt collection, including humiliating people publicly or intruding on the privacy of debtors' family members.
- **Harsh methods (para 91, microfinance loans):** Harsh conduct includes threatening or abusive language and persistently calling the borrower, including calls at inconvenient times. Full list not retrieved.
- **Recovery agent code (para 99):** NBFCs must get recovery agents' undertaking to follow the code of conduct, and agents must follow the Fair Practices Code and the NBFC's own collection and repossession code.
- **Agent due diligence (paras 93–94, microfinance):** Recovery agents are agencies and their employees, and NBFCs must run due diligence on them, including antecedent verification.
- **Undue harassment (para 20, Fair Practices Code):** NBFCs must not persistently bother borrowers at odd hours or use muscle power for recovery.
- **Borrower disclosure (Credit Facilities Directions, para 9(6), digital lending):** On default, the particulars of an assigned recovery agent must be communicated to the borrower.

content.text:
The corpus has the DPDP Rules 2025 notice requirements (Rule 3) and RBI digital-lending and recovery rules, but no DPDP Act consent provision and no rule that specifically addresses third-party contacts.

**What I found:**

- **DPDP Rules, Rule 3:** A notice to the borrower must be understandable on its own, and must give an itemised description of the personal data and the specified purpose. It must also give a link or other means to withdraw consent, exercise rights, and complain to the Board. Applied to contacts, the notice would need to itemise the contact-list data and the recovery purpose, which is my inference, not stated text.
- **RBI Credit Facilities Directions, para 13:** Any collection of data by an NBFC's digital lending app must be need-based and made with the borrower's prior and explicit consent, with an audit trail. Sharing with third parties is also regulated here. I only saw the opening of this paragraph, so I cannot confirm the full sharing conditions.
- **RBI Responsible Business Conduct Directions, paras 95–100:** Recovery agents must carry the NBFC's notice and authorisation letter and show their identity, and the NBFC must give the borrower the agent's details when recovery starts. Para 100 bars intimidation and intrusion on the privacy of debtors' family members, and para 91 treats persistent calling as harsh recovery. I only saw partial text of para 100.

**Gaps:**

- The corpus does not return the DPDP Act's consent and notice section (section 6), so I could not confirm the statutory consent standard the Rules rely on.
- Nothing I found addresses whether a non-consenting third party's number can be processed at all. The contact-list question for non-consenting third parties is therefore not answered by the corpus. Counsel should treat it as an open point, and it would be a reasonable inference that using a third party's number for recovery requires a lawful basis that the corpus does not establish.

findings.obligation: An NBFC must ensure its digital lending app (and its LSP's app) does not access mobile phone resources such as the contact list, call logs, files and media or telephony functions. Data collection must be need-based, with prior explicit consent and an audit trail. Only one-time camera, microphone or location access is allowed, and only for on-boarding/KYC.
findings.recommendation: Remove the contact-list permission from the app at sign-up. Audit all app permissions against the Para 13 list of prohibited resources. Delete any contact data already collected, and permit only one-time KYC-purpose access to camera, microphone or location.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: The borrower must be able to give or deny consent for specific data, restrict disclosure to third parties, set data retention, revoke consent already given and have the NBFC/LSP delete the data. The purpose of consent must be disclosed at each stage of interaction. Explicit consent is required before sharing personal information with third parties, unless a statutory or regulatory requirement applies.
findings.recommendation: Stop collecting contacts. Provide granular consent, revocation and deletion controls in the app. Do not use or share contact data with the recovery team or any third party without explicit borrower consent.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: The NBFC must ensure that it and its agents do not harass or intimidate any person in debt collection. This includes acts that intrude upon the privacy of the debtor's family members, referees and friends, and sending inappropriate messages by mobile or social media. Calling a borrower's contacts to disclose the debt is likely to breach this.
findings.recommendation: Stop recovery calls and messages to third parties in the borrower's contact list. Limit recovery communication to the borrower and any guarantor or co-borrower identified in the loan documents, and revise the recovery scripts and policy accordingly.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: Recovery must not involve undue harassment or persistently bothering borrowers at odd hours. Para 100 also bars calling the borrower before 8:00 a.m. and after 7:00 p.m. (this does not apply to microfinance loans). Recovery agents must be trained on hours of calling and privacy of customer information, and the NBFC must obtain their undertaking to abide by the code of conduct.
findings.recommendation: Enforce calling-hour limits and caps on call frequency in the recovery workflow. Train recovery agents on privacy and conduct. Obtain code-of-conduct undertakings from agents. Under Para 9(6) of the Digital Lending Directions, communicate the recovery agent's details to the borrower.

findings.obligation: Before consent is sought, the Data Fiduciary's notice must itemise the personal data to be processed and the specific purposes. It must also explain how to withdraw consent as easily as it was given, how to exercise rights, and how to complain to the Board. A notice and consent for the borrower's own data cannot cover third-party contacts who have received no notice.
findings.recommendation: Do not collect the contact list. If any personal data is collected, provide a standalone, itemised, purpose-specific notice with a withdrawal mechanism. Have privacy counsel assess the DPDP position on third-party contact data and on using data for recovery.

61. Secrecy Obligations and Sharing of Information:
(1) The NBFC shall maintain secrecy regarding the customer information that
arises out of the contractual relationship between the NBFC and the customer.
(2) The NBFC shall treat information collected from customers for the purpose of
opening of account as confidential and shall not divulge details thereof for the purpose
of cross-selling, or for any other purpose without the express permission of the
customer.
(3) While considering the requests for data / information from Government and
other agencies, the NBFC shall satisfy itself that the information being sought is not
of such a nature as will violate the provisions of the laws relating to secrecy in the
transactions.
(4) The exceptions to the said rule shall be as under:
(i) Where disclosure is under compulsion of law,
(ii) Where there is a duty to the public to disclose,
(iii) Where the interest of the NBFC requires disclosure, and
(iv) Where the disclosure is made with the express or implied consent of the
customer.

13. Collection, usage and sharing of data with third parties
(1) An NBFC shall ensure that any collection of data by their DLA and DLA of their
LSP is need-based and with prior and explicit consent of the borrower having
audit trail. In any case, an NBFC shall also ensure that DLA of NBFC / LSP
desist from accessing mobile phone resources like file and media, contact list,
call logs, telephony functions, etc. A one-time access can be taken for camera,
microphone, location or any other facility necessary for the purpose of on-
boarding / KYC requirements only, with the explicit consent of the borrower.
(2) The borrower shall be provided with an option to give or deny consent for use
of specific data, restrict disclosure to third parties, data retention, revoke
consent already granted to collect personal data and if required, make the
NBFC / LSP delete / forget the data.
(3) The purpose of obtaining borrowers’ consent needs to be disclosed at each
stage of interface with the borrowers.
(4) Explicit consent of the borrower shall be taken before sharing personal
information with any third party, except for cases where such sharing is
required as per statutory or regulatory requirement.
